pulls.title: Add "Agents on the Shared Message Bus" section on A2A
pulls.author: OR13
pulls.body:
## Summary

Elaborates on the utility of the **Shared Message Bus**, framing it as the first venue where agent-to-agent (A2A) collaboration surfaces in most organizations.

New top-level section **"Agents on the Shared Message Bus"** (placed after *Evolving Roles in Agentic Product Delivery*, before *Managing Your Agent*), making four points:

1. Organizations already run channels where people collaborate (IRC, Slack, Teams); Agents first arrive onto those existing channels.
2. Agents appear in two forms — as standalone identities, and acting on behalf of / impersonating the humans they serve (cross-references the Impersonation security section).
3. As Agents pursue business objectives they address one another: A2A is *already happening*, mediated by existing human communications platforms rather than a new agent-only protocol.
4. The benefit is legibility — non-technical stakeholders can follow, contribute to, and review these discussions without special tooling.

Also adds an explicit `{#impersonation}` anchor to the Impersonation heading so the new section can cross-reference it.

## Points for review

- **Placement** — I put this as a standalone top-level section between *Evolving Roles* and *Managing Your Agent*. Alternatives: fold into *Managing Your People* (which already discusses the bus + Proxy Dictation), or place earlier as foundational context. Easy to move.
- **"A2A" as prose vs. defined term** — introduced inline as "agent-to-agent (A2A)" rather than as a capitalized Terminology entry. If A2A should become a formal defined Term, say so.
- **A2A-protocol framing** — the closing contrasts reusing human channels with a hypothetical "agent-only protocol." Kept descriptive (a trade-off, not a verdict) to avoid appearing to disparage emerging A2A protocol work. Flag if you want it more/less pointed.

## Build

Rebuilds clean via `kramdown-rfc` + `xml2rfc` (the `make` venv is currently broken locally — see note below); `{{impersonation}}` resolves to the real section anchor. Only the pre-existing `[1m]` link-ID warning remains, unrelated to this change.

> Note: `make` fails locally because `lib/.venv` points at a broken Python. The build was verified by invoking `kramdown-rfc` / `xml2rfc` directly. Happy to open a separate PR to repair the venv if useful.

pulls.title: Add self-identifying marker (shibboleth) subsection on impersonation
pulls.author: OR13
pulls.body:
## Summary

Adds a concrete, prompt-based mitigation for the impersonation risk on shared channels: a new subsection **"A Shibboleth for Agent-Generated Content"** under *Agents on the Shared Message Bus*.

The mitigation: instruct the Agent, in its persistent Context, to prefix **every** message with a fixed, conspicuous marker, so any reader can tell at a glance the content was generated by an Agent rather than written by the human whose channel it shares. Illustrated with a real team member's rule:

> `omg bestie <short, appropriate opener> 💅`

The subsection then relates the pattern to a **Shibboleth** (new informative reference to the Wikipedia article), noting it *inverts* the classical use — historically a shibboleth proved in-group membership; here it is a tell the Agent emits to mark itself as machine-generated. It closes with the limits, which reinforce the existing **Impersonation** security section: a convention-only marker is a cooperative signal, not an authenticated one — an Agent may drop it (error, Context Rot) and an adversary can trivially forge it — so it `MUST NOT` be relied on as proof of authorship; the platform controls in `{{impersonation}}` remain necessary under adversarial conditions.

## Editorial choices for review

- **Placement** — added as a `##` subsection of the *Agents on the Shared Message Bus* section (merged in #1), rather than in the *Impersonation* security section, to keep the Security Considerations' normative language uncluttered while giving the concrete example room. Cross-linked both ways. Easy to relocate into Security Considerations if you'd prefer.
- **Genericized the colleague's name** — your example named "Justin"; I replaced it with "the human I work for" to avoid putting a real individual's name in a published I-D. Kept the authentic first-person voice and the literal `💅` marker otherwise verbatim. Say the word if you'd rather name them (or use a placeholder like `<manager>`).
- **Literal emoji** — the draft is `v: 3`, so the 💅 builds clean in both HTML and text output (verified, no new warnings). If a future ASCII-only rendering is a concern we can switch to a described form.

## Build

Rebuilds clean via `kramdown-rfc` + `xml2rfc` (HTML and text); `{{SHIBBOLETH}}` and both `{{impersonation}}` cross-references resolve. Only the pre-existing `[1m]` link-ID warning remains, unrelated to this change. (`make` itself is still blocked by the broken `lib/.venv`.)

pulls.title: Retitle to "Vibeslop Confessions" and write the Introduction
pulls.author: OR13
pulls.body:
## Summary

Two related changes to the front of the draft:

- **Title:** `Vibeslop` → `Vibeslop Confessions` (title-cased to match RFC convention; ping if you'd prefer lowercase).
- **Introduction:** replaces the `TODO Introduction` stub with prose framing the document as assembled from first-hand accounts — interviews with people building software with AI Agents, plus direct experimentation in new ways of working that support agentic software delivery.

The Introduction establishes the document's register (descriptive and candid, not prescriptive), explains the "confessions" framing, notes that normative language captures practitioner-valued guidance rather than agreed standards, and presents the document as a snapshot expected to age quickly — consistent with the abstract.

## Verification

- `kramdown-rfc draft-steele-vibeslop.md` processes cleanly (exit 0). The lone `link ID '1m'` warning is pre-existing in the Acknowledgments (`claude-opus-4-8[1m]`), untouched here.
- `make` currently fails in this environment due to a stale pinned Python venv (unrelated to these edits).
- Branched off `main`; independent of open PR #2 (shibboleth marker).

Requesting mutual review before merge — please do not squash-merge without @MJL40635 sign-off.
